sections.h2: Selling in Miami Lakes: the basics
sections.html:
Miami Lakes is a planned town in northwest Miami-Dade County, and the planning shapes how its houses sell. Population is near 31,240, spread over roughly 6.5 square miles, with about 4,720 businesses inside the town limits. It sits 16 miles north of Downtown Miami and about 10 miles from Miami International Airport, which is the commute story most buyers hear first.

The town runs from NW 170th Street and the Palmetto Expressway on the north to NW 138th Street on the south, and from NW 57th Avenue (Red Road) on the east to Interstate 75 on the west.

Because so much of the town sits inside one master plan, a seller here usually runs into a homeowners association, a lake or canal frontage question, or a special taxing district earlier than sellers in older grid suburbs do. Sort out which of those apply to your address before you talk to any buyer.

sections.h2: What the master plan means for your house
sections.html:
The original plan covered 3,000 acres of former dairy land and produced winding streets, cul-de-sacs, 23 lakes, parks and separate business parks. Buyers see all of that on a drive-by, so curb appeal, tree condition and the state of the swale count for more than usual. Light industrial and office parks take up about 13 percent of the town, and lakes and canals about 11 percent.

  • Housing ranges from medium-density multifamily to large waterfront single-family homes, with many lakefront townhouse communities.
  • Most of the town is low density, with a Town Center and parks spread between neighborhoods.
  • The town's businesses employ about 30,000 people, and only 12 percent of those workers live in Miami Lakes.

If your home is a townhouse or sits in an association, ask for the current dues, any pending assessments and the estoppel procedure early. Those papers take time, and a buyer's lender will want them.

sections.h2: Drainage, guarded districts and town projects
sections.html:
Miami-Dade Fire Rescue answers calls here, mainly from the Miami Lakes station and the Miami Lakes West station, which together handled about 89 percent of responses in fiscal 2025. There were 3,546 emergency calls to the town that year.

Drainage work is the item an owner is most likely to notice. Finished projects include Canal Bank Stabilization Phase III and the Francesca Mary and Loch Lomond drainage improvements. Many neighborhood jobs are still under way, among them Royal Oaks additions and West Lakes Phase IV. If your street is on a project list, tell the buyer what was done and ask the Town for the project status in writing.

A house inside one of the Town's special taxing districts carries extra costs, such as automated gate arms and guardhouse work, and buyers tend to raise them. Pull the district charge from your tax bill so you can answer without guessing.

The Town also runs the FreeBee on-demand ride service, which gave more than 28,564 rides in the year, and it launched a Vision Zero plan for road safety.

sections.h2: What a Miami Lakes listing can highlight
sections.html:
Fiscal 2025 gave sellers several facts a listing can lean on. Emergency response times ran under 6.5 minutes, and the Town ranked among the top three safest cities in Miami-Dade County in a Niche report. Police figures show a 45 percent drop in auto thefts and a 73 percent drop in residential and commercial burglaries. The fiscal year ran October 1, 2024 through September 30, 2025, so date any number you quote.

  • Parks: Royal Oaks Park fields, K9 Cove, a marina on the C8 canal and pocket parks renovated with new benches and signs.
  • Recreation: more than 1,800 registrants in youth and adult leagues, tennis and pickleball programs, and an archery program.
  • Events: a Fourth of July celebration and Main Street Live in the Town Center.
  • Transit: free on-demand FreeBee rides within town limits.

sections.h2: Deed stamp tax and recording fees
sections.html:
Florida charges a documentary stamp tax on deeds, and Miami-Dade is the one county with a different schedule. The state holds everyone named on the document liable, whichever side agrees to pay, so the contract should say who covers it.

Deed documentary stamp tax by location
Where the property isRate on a deed
Counties other than Miami-Dade70 cents per $100 or portion thereof
Miami-Dade County60 cents per $100, plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax
Surtax exceptionNot due on a document transferring only a single-family dwelling

Miami Lakes has many lakefront townhouses and multifamily units, so ask your closing agent which line fits your property type. The clerk takes the tax at the moment the deed is recorded and adds page-based recording fees under section 28.24.

Property tax comes on its own bill. The Town's annual performance report charts millage for Miami-Dade municipalities, and the Miami-Dade tax collector can give you the current Miami Lakes rate. A web-based millage calculator from the Town lets residents compare this year's taxes with last year's. The Town's rate is just a piece of the total, since the county, school board and special districts each add theirs.

Have the closing agent split the year between you and the buyer, and hold back money for the November bill when it is not out yet at closing. Expect the buyer's first bill to run well above yours.

sections.h2: Florida tax dates and homestead rules
sections.html:
Miami Lakes homeowners pay county, school, Town and special district charges on one November bill. The calendar comes from the state: values are fixed as of January 1, a proposed-tax notice arrives in August, and bills land in November with an early-payment discount that shrinks from 4 percent to 1 percent by February.

  • Homestead applications reach the Miami-Dade appraiser by March 1, on Form DR-501.
  • Homestead status ends if you rent the home out or move away.
  • Save Our Homes caps yearly assessment growth on a homestead. After a sale the assessment jumps to market-based just value at the next first of January.
  • To contest a value, file with the clerk within 25 days of the August mailing. Unpaid bills turn delinquent April 1.

sections.h2: What is the fastest way to sell in Miami Lakes?
sections.html:
You can hire a broker, sell it yourself, or take a cash bid from an investor. Each route gives up something different for speed. Lakefront and gated-district homes tend to draw financed buyers, while a dated interior or a deferred drainage problem can favor an as-is investor.

  • Agent listing: most exposure to financed buyers, with repair requests after the inspection.
  • Owner-marketed sale: no listing fee, but you write the contract and handle showings and disclosures.
  • Investor bid: fewer contingencies and a closing date set by you, at a discount for speed.

A cash sale avoids the lender's appraisal, the loan approval and most repair haggling. The title search, the deed and the stamp tax still happen. Collect offers in writing, ask every bidder who pays for title work and stamps, and let an attorney or closing agent review the contract first.

After you accept an offer, the title company hunts for liens, open permits and unpaid taxes. Have ready the deed, a mortgage payoff figure, the latest tax bill, the association's contact details and any special taxing district paperwork. At the signing table you execute the deed before witnesses or a notary, and the clerk records it and collects the tax.

With a tenant in place, hand over the lease so the buyer sees the term and the rent.

Foreclosure in Florida goes through a judge. After final judgment the clerk schedules a public auction 20 to 35 days out, though the lender can agree to wait longer. The top bidder puts down 5 percent, and objections to the bid are due ten days after the certificate of sale. Selling privately ahead of that auction lets you keep any equity.

Heirs can use summary administration, a shortened court process, when the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less or the owner died more than two years ago. Creditors lose their claims after the longer of three months from first publication or 30 days from service. Florida collects no estate tax return for deaths after 2004.

Someone living there unlawfully who is not a tenant can be removed by the sheriff after the owner files a verified complaint under section 82.036, if the statute's conditions are met. For a leaseholder behind on rent, a three-day written notice comes before any eviction suit.

faqs.q: How long does a Miami Lakes sale take to close?
faqs.a: With clean title a cash deal can finish in a few weeks. A financed buyer adds inspection, appraisal and lender steps. A title defect, a lien or a slow association approval can hold up either one.

faqs.q: Who pays the documentary stamp tax on a Miami Lakes deed?
faqs.a: Your contract assigns the cost, but the state treats all parties to the document as liable. Miami-Dade charges 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax, and a deed for only a single-family dwelling skips the surtax.

faqs.q: Does a sale reset my property tax assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. The new owner starts at full market-based value as of the next first of January and gets none of your Save Our Homes cap. Transfers between spouses and some transfers at death are exceptions.

faqs.q: Is a home inside a guarded Miami Lakes district harder to sell?
faqs.a: It can be, since buyers see the district charge and any gate or guardhouse costs. Ask the Town and the Miami-Dade tax collector for current amounts before you set a price.

faqs.q: Who files the deed after a Miami Lakes sale?
faqs.a: Your title company usually submits it to the Miami-Dade court clerk, who takes the stamp tax and page charges in the same step.
